title: Bad-Pass Catching
description: The coach throws deliberately imperfect passes — low, high, behind — and receivers must secure them, preparing for the real passes they get in games.

content.objective: Catch and secure off-target passes by moving the feet to the ball and using two hands.
content.setup: Coach at the top of the key; players in a line at the wing.
content.organization: One player at a time; catch, secure, shoot or pass back.
instructions: The player cuts to the wing and shows a target.
The coach throws a pass that is low, high, wide or behind.
The player moves the feet to get the body behind the ball and catches with two hands.
After securing, the player squares up and shoots.
coachingPoints: Move the feet first, then the hands.
Two hands on every catch, even when stretching.
commonMistakes: Reaching with one hand and fumbling.
Giving up on a bad pass.
Rushing the shot before the ball is secure.
content.safety: Passes are imperfect but not thrown hard at the body or face.
progressions: Add a defender who contests the catch.
Player must catch on the move and finish.
regressions: Tell the player which pass is coming.
variations: Use a medicine ball for the first rounds (strength).
Catch in the post with a defender on the back.
content.gameApplication: Game passes are rarely perfect; players who catch them keep possessions alive.
